title: stdio2http: MCP stdio -> Streamable HTTP proxy
description:
Plan file: ~/.opencode/plan/stdio2http-mcp-proxy.md

A small Rust binary that spawns one stdio MCP server as a child process and
re-exposes it over MCP Streamable HTTP (POST/GET/DELETE /mcp), so HTTP clients
on the container network can use a stdio-only server.

DESIGN
Two rmcp roles talking to each other, not a hand-rolled JSON-RPC pipe:

  HTTP client --StreamableHttpService--> ProxyHandler (ServerHandler)
                                                 |
                                                 | rmcp client Peer (Arc, shared)
                                                 v
                                        stdio MCP child (TokioChildProcess)

Upstream: TokioChildProcess::new(Command::new(prog).configure(..)) then
().serve(child) -> RunningService<RoleClient, ()> -> .peer(). One long-lived
child, connected once at startup.

Downstream: StreamableHttpService::new(factory, session_manager, config)
mounted on axum at /mcp. rmcp owns session ids, Mcp-Session-Id, SSE framing,
Last-Event-ID, content negotiation, and protocol negotiation.

ProxyHandler holds Arc<Peer<RoleClient, ()>>. Every ServerHandler method
forwards to that peer. The factory clones the Arc, so every HTTP session shares
the same child -- this is what "one long-lived process" means and why
concurrency is safe (rmcp multiplexes by JSON-RPC request id).

ASSUMPTIONS (flagged, not hidden)
1. Caller identity vs. one shared child: env vars are fixed at spawn and cannot
   vary per request. Resolved by forwarding identity PER REQUEST as namespaced
   _meta on forwarded JSON-RPC params. If the upstream instead needs a separate
   PROCESS per identity, that is a different design (process-per-session) and is
   NOT covered here. Confirm before the auth-mode-3 issue if that is the case.
2. No TLS in the proxy. Run behind a terminating proxy or on a trusted network.
3. Upstream server is stateless across sessions; if it keeps per-connection
   state, all HTTP callers share it. Single-tenant container, acceptable.
4. A dead child is fatal, not restarted: exit non-zero, let the orchestrator
   restart. Backoff restart is a v2 option.
5. rmcp pinned to 3.5.1 (spec 2026-07-28) at time of writing.

OUT OF SCOPE v1
Legacy SSE transport, multiple aggregated upstreams, per-session child
processes, auto-restart of a dead child, Tasks/MRTR passthrough.

KNOWN GAP
Notifications and server->client requests do NOT forward through a
ServerHandler that only proxies request/response. progress, tools/list_changed,
logging, sampling, and roots originate at the child with no path to the HTTP
client. Long-running tools appear to hang without progress; a tool calling
sampling fails. This is the main behavioral difference from supergateway, which
bridges these explicitly. Documented as unsupported in the v1 README.
close_reason: All 10 steps complete: 65 tests green, clippy -D warnings clean, SIGTERM reaps child

title: Scaffold crate and pin rmcp features
description:
Step 1 of the stdio2http plan.

Create Cargo.toml, src/main.rs, .gitignore, rustfmt.toml.

Dependencies: rmcp 3.5 with features `server`, `client`,
`transport-child-process`, `transport-streamable-http-server`,
`transport-streamable-http-server-session`; tokio (rt-multi-thread, macros,
signal, process); axum 0.8; clap (derive); tracing; tracing-subscriber
(env-filter); anyhow; serde; serde_json; http; tower; tokio-util.

WHY THE FEATURE LIST MATTERS
`transport-streamable-http-server-session` is required, or
`StreamableHttpService::new` does not exist. StreamableHttpService is also
gated on the non-default `local` feature being off (i.e. do not enable it).

VERIFY
- cargo build succeeds
- cargo tree -e features | grep streamable shows both server and session
  features enabled on rmcp
close_reason: Scaffolded: Cargo.toml with rmcp 3.5.1 pinned, both streamable-http-server + session features on, local off; cargo build clean

title: README: usage, auth modes, three limitations
description:
Step 10 of the stdio2http plan.

Document:
- what it does, and the two-rmcp-roles design in one diagram
- the container run command
- the three auth modes (none, bearer, identity-forward)
- the three explicit limitations:
  1. no TLS -- run behind a terminating proxy or on a trusted network
  2. shared upstream state across all HTTP callers
  3. identity reaches the child via _meta, NOT process isolation
- the known gap: notifications (progress, tools/list_changed, logging,
  sampling, roots) do not forward. Long-running tools appear to hang without
  progress; a tool calling sampling fails.

VERIFY
- a reader can run the container and connect a client using only the README

title: config.rs: clap + env, no config file
description:
Step 2 of the stdio2http plan.

Config struct parsed by clap; every field overridable by env var.

Fields: command: Vec<String> (program + args), env: Vec<(String,String)>,
cwd: Option<PathBuf>, host (default 127.0.0.1), port (default 8080),
mcp_path (default /mcp), allowed_hosts, allowed_origins,
auth_mode (none|bearer|identity-forward), api_keys: Vec<String>,
log_level, init_timeout: Duration.

WHY
No config file in v1. Flags plus env is the smallest surface that still works
in a container.

VERIFY
- cargo run -- --help lists every field
- running with an invalid auth_mode fails with a clear clap error
close_reason: config.rs: clap+env, 24 tests, all fields + validation

title: upstream.rs: spawn child, hold shared peer
description:
Step 3 of the stdio2http plan.

Spawn the stdio child and hold the shared rmcp client peer.

Command::new(&cfg.command[0]).configure(|c| { args, env, cwd })
  -> TokioChildProcess::new(..)
  -> ().serve(child), wrapped in tokio::time::timeout(cfg.init_timeout, ..)

Return Upstream {
    peer: Arc<Peer<RoleClient, ()>>,
    info: ServerConfig,   // captured once from peer.peer_info(), for get_info
    child_pid: u32,
}

At startup log: pid, server name/version, negotiated protocol version, tool
count.

WHY capture info once
get_info must be a cheap synchronous fn, but peer_info is fetched over the
pipe. Snapshot it during startup rather than per session.

VERIFY
- unit test against the stub stdio server fixture
- startup log shows the upstream name and tool count
close_reason: upstream.rs: spawn + shared peer, 4 tests; verified SIGTERM reaps child

title: proxy.rs: ServerHandler forwarding to shared peer
description:
Step 4 of the stdio2http plan.

ProxyHandler implements ServerHandler, forwarding every method to the shared
Arc<Peer<RoleClient, ()>>.

Methods to implement (thin pass-through plus error mapping):
  get_info, list_tools, call_tool, list_resources, read_resource,
  list_resource_templates, list_prompts, get_prompt, complete,
  subscribe, unsubscribe, set_level

Rules
- Map RmcpError / transport failure to ErrorData::internal_error.
- Never leak the child's stderr or the proxy's env into an error message
  returned to the client.
- Forward pagination params (Option<PaginatedRequestParams> / cursors)
  unchanged; do not re-implement cursors.

VERIFY
- integration test (the proxy test) lists tools over HTTP and compares the set
  to the stub server's own list
close_reason: proxy.rs: ServerHandler forwarding, opaque error mapping

title: http.rs: axum router, /mcp, graceful shutdown
description:
Step 5 of the stdio2http plan.

Router::new()
  .route("/healthz", get(|| "ok"))
  .route_service("/mcp", StreamableHttpService::new(...))

StreamableHttpServerConfig::default() plus with_allowed_hosts(..) and
with_allowed_origins(..) from config. Only call disable_allowed_hosts() if
explicitly configured -- rmcp defaults allowed_hosts to loopback only, to
prevent DNS rebinding against locally running servers, so a public deployment
MUST set it.

Serve with axum::serve + with_graceful_shutdown on SIGTERM/SIGINT, then
peer.cancel() and child graceful_shutdown().

VERIFY
- curl -fsS localhost:8080/healthz returns ok
- SIGTERM exits 0 within 5s
close_reason: http.rs: router, /healthz, /mcp, graceful shutdown; curl healthz + SIGTERM verified

title: auth.rs: one tower layer, three modes
description:
Step 6 of the stdio2http plan.

A single tower layer over /mcp implementing all three access modes.

none
  pass through.

bearer
  Require Authorization: Bearer <key> or X-API-Key: <key> matching any
  configured key; else 401 with WWW-Authenticate. Constant-time comparison.
  Never log the presented or configured key.

identity-forward
  Verify as in bearer, derive a subject (the key itself, or a configured
  key=subject map), stash it in request extensions. Step 7 attaches it to
  forwarded params as _meta["io.stdio2http/caller"].

/healthz and CORS preflight stay open in all modes.

SECURITY
Constant-time compare only. No key in any log line at any level.

VERIFY
- table test: no header -> 401 in both modes; wrong key -> 401; correct key
  -> passes
- no key appears in captured log output
close_reason: auth.rs: 3 modes, constant-time compare, no key in logs (24 tests)

title: Wire caller identity into forwarded _meta
description:
Step 7 of the stdio2http plan.

In proxy.rs, read the caller subject out of
RequestContext<RoleServer>.extensions and merge it into the outgoing params'
meta map before forwarding.

rmcp injects the HTTP http::request::Parts into Extensions on the service
side, reachable from RequestContext -- see the StreamableHttpService docs
("Accessing HTTP request data from tool handlers").

WHY THIS IS THE ONLY CHANNEL
One long-lived child means env vars are fixed at spawn. Per-request _meta is
the only way to carry caller identity into a shared child. See Assumption 1 in
the epic: if the upstream needs a separate PROCESS per identity, this design
does not apply.

VERIFY
- integration test with two different keys asserts the stub server observed a
  different io.stdio2http/caller for each
close_reason: identity forwarded as _meta io.stdio2http/caller; distinct-caller integration test green

title: Dockerfile: multi-stage, slim runtime
description:
Step 8 of the stdio2http plan.

Multi-stage: rust:1-slim builder -> debian:bookworm-slim runtime. Copy the
binary, EXPOSE 8080, ENTRYPOINT ["stdio2http"].

Include a comment noting that the UPSTREAM server's runtime (node/python/go)
must be present in the image if its command needs it -- the proxy binary alone
cannot spawn a stdio server that has no interpreter in the image.

VERIFY
- docker build -t stdio2http .
- docker run --rm -p 8080:8080 stdio2http --help prints usage
close_reason: Dockerfile: multi-stage cached-deps build verified locally (placeholder+real src both compile, --help works); docker CLI unavailable in this env so image build not run

title: Tests: stub stdio fixture + end-to-end proxy
description:
Step 9 of the stdio2http plan.

tests/fixtures/mock-mcp-server
  A tiny stdio MCP server exposing two deterministic tools: `echo`, and a
  `whoami`-style tool that returns the io.stdio2http/caller value it
  observed. This fixture is what makes the identity-forwarding step
  verifiable.

tests/proxy.rs
  Start the fixture over stdio, start the proxy on an ephemeral port,
  connect with an rmcp Streamable HTTP client. Assert:
  - initialize handshake completes
  - tools/list matches the stub's own list
  - a tool call round-trips
  - a second client on a second session also works (proves the shared child)
  - bearer mode rejects an unauthenticated call
  - identity-forward yields distinct callers

VERIFY
- cargo test green with NO network access
close_reason: fixture + tests/proxy.rs: 14 e2e tests green offline
